$comment: The Microtone design system's component manifest and rules, for people and for tools. Hand-written; test/node/design-system.test.js checks that every module under components/ is listed, that every export named here exists, that every class named here is styled in microtone.css, and that every token named here exists in tokens.json. Read design-system/README.md first.
name: Microtone

library.import: Import a component by its REAL path (../components/actions.js from src/ui/popups/). The design-system/components link is for reading; a module loaded through it resolves its own imports (../i18n.js) against the link and breaks.

rules.title: Dialog actions: Cancel left, Proceed right
rules.text: Every dialog's action row is built by actionRow(). Cancel sits at the LEFT end (Esc does the same). Proceed — the one action the dialog is for — sits at the RIGHT end (Enter does the same where the dialog has typed fields). Non-cancelling alternatives (Preview, Record, Import as new, Clear) are PREPENDED to Proceed: immediately left of it, in the right-hand group. A dialog with nothing to commit and nothing to abandon (About, a notice, a finished log, a panel whose edits apply live) has ONE Dismiss button at the right end, and neither Cancel nor Proceed. DOM order equals visual order equals Tab order.
exceptions: The Analogue Warmth Edition's splash (popups/warmth.js) is a parody advert with its own centred button.

rules.title: Proceed is the one coloured, heavier button
rules.text: The Proceed button (class `proceed`) is filled with proceed-bg (the accent) and inked proceed-fg; its label is set at weight-proceed, at least 200 heavier than weight-button. No other button is filled with the accent or heavier (the armed Record toggle wears its own red: a state, not an action). Microtone Touch's `.tbtn.primary` is the same thing under its own name.

rules.title: Every colour is a token
rules.text: Every colour in the app, DOM and canvas alike, is a custom property declared on :root in microtone.css once per theme (dark, dim, light, warmth). Canvas views read them through src/ui/theme.js. Never hard-code a colour in a view, a popup or an inline style: reuse a token or add one (in all four themes, with a note in design-system/notes.json or a trailing comment), then run node tools/design-tokens.js.

rules.title: One meaning per hue
rules.text: accent is focus, hover, 'this one is active' and Proceed; accent-2 is instruments, links and selection; meter is level and liveness; rec-fg is record armed. Don't borrow one for decoration. Colours that must be told apart differ in lightness, not hue alone.

rules.title: Native form controls are themed centrally
rules.text: :root { accent-color: var(--accent) } paints every checkbox, radio, range slider and <progress>. Never restate accent-color on a widget. A control that cannot be native (a canvas fader, a custom switch) paints itself from var(--accent).

rules.title: Faces by token, never by name
rules.text: Chrome is Open Sans (narrowed, tabular figures); the wordmark alone is Geist. Every monospace is a Motif face through its token: --cv-font (Motif Grid: grids and notes as symbols), --mono-font (Motif Mono: values someone types or reads), --transport-font (Motif Transport), --code-font (Motif Code). Never a bare `monospace`, Chivo Mono or Roboto Mono.

rules.title: A note outside the grids is text
rules.text: Spell a note with noteGlyph()/rangeGlyph() (components/noteglyph.js): a .note-glyph span in --cv-font, in the song's own notation. Never draw a note into a small DOM canvas.

rules.title: Panels fold to their titlebar
rules.text: A panel that can fold is built with makeFoldable() (components/fold.js): a caret twisty at the LEFT end of its titlebar, pointing down while open and right while shut, and the panel's name beside it as a second pointer target (the twisty alone is in the Tab order). Only the BODY folds: the titlebar's own controls — a switch, a Mix slider, a readout — stay live while the panel is shut. Folding is never an undo step. Where the panel's subject is saved in the project and the format has a place for the fold (an IMix equipment's folded flag, beside its bypass — TAUD_FILE_FORMAT.md §9.15) the state is saved there through get/set; otherwise it is the viewer's, in localStorage per kind of panel (key). A panel nobody has touched takes the caller's default — open what is in use, shut what is not.

rules.title: Write the DOM only on change
rules.text: The frame loop visits every open view 60 times a second: compare before writing textContent, never read layout after a write in the same frame, and repaint canvases on change (gridKey/restKey), not on schedule.

rules.title: Words
rules.text: Plain, exact British English (colour, centre). Sentence case for buttons, menus and titles; uppercase only in tab labels. An ellipsis (…) on a label means a dialog follows. No exclamation marks, no emoji. One of the parts a song is written on is a LANE (never a channel or voice in prose). Effect codes in docs: `S $7300` — opcode, no-break space, dollar sign, argument, in backticks.

components.name: ActionRow
components.summary: The button row at the foot of every dialog, laid out by role: Cancel at the left end, extras and alternatives, Proceed at the right end — or one Dismiss at the right end.
components.api: actionRow({ cancel?, alternatives?: spec[], proceed?, dismiss?, extras?: Node[], className? }) → { row, cancel, proceed, dismiss, alternatives }. A spec is a label string, true (the role's default label: Cancel / Close), or { label, icon, iconAfter, title, className, disabled }. dismiss throws beside cancel or proceed.
components.example:
const { row, cancel, proceed } = actionRow({ cancel: true, alternatives: [{ label: t("chord.preview"), icon: "play" }], proceed: t("chord.apply") });
dlg.append(row);

components.name: Modal
components.summary: A form dialog on a native <dialog>, built from field specs: captions in one column, controls ending on one right edge, hints under their field; resolves with the values or null. showNotice is its one-button sibling for something only to be read.
components.api: showModal({ title, body?, fields: [{ name, label, type?: 'text'|'number'|'select'|'checkbox', value?, options?, min?, max?, placeholder?, hint?, hints?, enabledWhen?: { field, is? | not? }, select? }], okLabel }) → Promise<values|null>. showNotice({ title, body?, okLabel }) → Promise<void>.
components.example:
const r = await showModal({ title: t("files.renameTitle", { name: old }), fields: [{ name: "name", label: t("files.name"), value: old }], okLabel: t("common.rename") });
if (!r) return; // Cancel, Esc

components.name: ValueControl
components.summary: Every number field and dropdown as a three-segment group: the native control in the middle, − and + (or ‹ and ›) step buttons either side, one hairline round the three that turns accent on focus. The native element is kept, so call sites need nothing.
components.api: Automatic: startControlEnhancer() upgrades every <input type=number> and <select> as views build them; opt one out with data-mt="off". mapSpinner(input, { toDisplay, fromDisplay, step }, raw) shows a stored value in other units (seconds, dB, hex).

components.name: ContextMenu
components.summary: The icon-cell menu pinned to the pointer: rows of square cells, an icon over a caption; exactly one highlighted cell, moved alike by the arrows and the pointer.
components.api: showContextMenu(x, y, rows: [[{ id, label, icon, title?, disabled? }]], { keyboard? }) → Promise<id|null>. icon is inline SVG from icons.js ICON.

components.name: DragGrip
components.summary: A drag handle that reorders sibling rows in place, by pointer (mouse and touch) or by ↑ ↓ on the focused grip; the reorder commits once, on release.
components.api: dragGrip({ index, count, rowSel = 'tr', title, onMove(from, to, via) }) → <button>. focusGrip(root, index) after a re-render.

components.name: Fold
components.summary: Folds a titlebar-over-body panel shut to its titlebar: a caret twisty at the left end, the name as a second target, the state kept by the caller (in the project) or per viewer under a key.
components.api: makeFoldable(box, { head, body, name?, get?(), set?(open), key?, open = true, label?, onToggle?(open) }) → { toggle, isOpen(), setOpen(open), sync() }. get/set keep the state in the caller's model (sync() after it moved underneath); key keeps it in localStorage. foldOpen(key, fallback) reads a stored state.
components.example: const fold = makeFoldable(unit, { head, body, name, label: t("imix.foldTitle"), get: () => !piece.folded, set: (open) => doc.setImixFolded(chain, id, !open) });

components.name: NoteGlyph
components.summary: A note spelled exactly as the grids spell it — the song's own notation, Kite ticks, lü, off-grid ink — as ordinary text in Motif Grid.
components.api: noteGlyph(note, preset) → <span class=note-glyph>. rangeGlyph(lo, hi, preset, wholeText). noteRun(items, preset): numbers are notes, strings dim separators.

components.name: Button
components.summary: The one pushbutton: a panel-2 key, a border hairline, radius-md corners, the border turning accent on hover. A plain <button> gets it all; there is no .btn class.
components.api: <button> · button.big (the one primary action of a page) · .icon-btn (icon only, top bar) · .proceed (a dialog's Proceed — use actionRow) · .rec / .rec.on (record arm) · an icon first as <svg class=btn-ico> from icons.js (btn-ico after for a trailing arrow).

components.name: Badge
components.summary: A small status chip: err-fg on err-bg, or ok-fg on ok-bg with .on; .sel-mode is the outlined accent-2 chip of block-selection mode. The text says the state; colour never carries it alone.
components.api: Audio off · Audio on · SEL

components.name: Tabs
components.summary: The pane tab strip: uppercase labels on panel-2 keys rounded at the top; the active tab fills with bg and inks accent, joining the view below.
components.api:
…
· .subtabs for the smaller in-panel strip.

components.name: Toolbar
components.summary: The app's bars — top bar, toolbox, command palette, status bar — one strip on panel ruled from the view by a border hairline.
components.api: .topbar (wordmark, transport, globals; .tb-sep rules, .grow pushes right) · .toolbox (the view's tools, .active) · .cmd-palette (.pal-label, buttons, .pal-hint) · .statusbar (.pos pairs: a dim caption and an fg value).

components.name: Wordmark
components.summary: The typeset name: 'Micro' in brand, 'tone' in brand2, Geist 900 oblique, a dim superscript TM drawn by CSS.
components.api: Microtone inside .brand-container (top bar) or .wc-brand (welcome). Never recolour a half, set it upright, or type the TM.
